author: austinamorusoyardstick
body:
This pull request refactors the processing of pull request comments to improve logging, streamline the flow, and enhance the prompt formatting. The most important changes include adding more descriptive logging, modifying the `formatCommentAsPrompt` method to include additional context, and simplifying the comment processing logic.

### Logging improvements:
* Added detailed logging to indicate when a comment is skipped due to an empty prompt and improved clarity in log messages by including the total number of comments being processed.
* Enhanced the prompt preview logging to provide a clearer summary of the prompt content being sent to Claude.

### Prompt formatting enhancements:
* Updated the `formatCommentAsPrompt` method to include the comment index, total number of comments, and additional context such as the number of accepted pieces for split comments. This provides more informative prompts for processing.

### Code simplification:
* Removed unnecessary test message logic and redundant delays in the `processCommentsSequentially` method, reducing complexity and improving efficiency.
* Adjusted the delay logic to only apply between comments, ensuring smoother processing without unnecessary pauses after the last comment.

body:
## Summary
• Improved GitHub Actions workflow for PyPI deployment with better debugging
• Enhanced setuptools-scm configuration for cleaner version generation
• Added verbose output and version information display for troubleshooting

## Changes Made

### GitHub Actions Workflow Improvements
- Added `verbose: true` and `print-hash: true` to PyPI publishing steps
- Added version information display step showing:
  - Git describe output
  - Exact tag matching status  
  - setuptools-scm generated version
- This helps debug version generation and deployment issues

### setuptools-scm Configuration
- Tested various version schemes and local schemes
- Identified that clean release versions require exact tag matches
- Improved understanding of version generation process

## Version Generation Insights
The key to getting clean version numbers (e.g., `0.2.4` instead of `0.2.4.dev0+hash`) is:
1. Tag must be created on the exact commit that will be built
2. No uncommitted changes when building
3. Tag should represent the final release state

## Next Steps
After merging, we can:
1. Create a proper release tag on main branch
2. Test the complete PyPI deployment workflow
3. Verify clean version generation

## Test plan
- ✅ Workflow syntax validated
- ✅ setuptools-scm configuration tested locally
- ✅ Version generation behavior analyzed
- 🔄 Full deployment test pending merge and release

author: rtfeldman
body:
Now the same source code leads to the exact same serialized bytes regardless of what CPU architecture it's being built on (or any other factor for that matter). This means that you can now serialize on a Roc compiler running on wasm32, send those serialized bytes to a Roc compiler running on aarch64 (or vice versa) and everything will Just Work.

I did a proof-of-concept and LLVM optimizes this to essentially the same thing as before on 64-bit targets. It's slightly less efficient on 32-bit targets, but nothing serious - just writing various struct fields into different locations versus them already being in exactly the desired location already.

body:
This PR updates [pip](https://pypi.org/project/pip) from **19.0.3** to **25.2**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 25.2
   ```
   =================

Features
--------

- Declare support for Python 3.14 (`13506 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13506>`_)
- Automatic download resumption and retrying is enabled by default. (`13464 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13464>`_)
- Requires-Python error message displays version clauses in numerical order. (`13367 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13367>`_)
- Minor performance improvement getting the order to install a very large number of interdependent packages. (`13424 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13424>`_)
- Show time taken instead of ``eta 0:00:00`` at download completion. (`13483 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13483>`_)
- Speed up small CLI tools by removing ``import re`` from the console
  script executable template. (`13165 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13165>`_)
- Remove warning when cloning from a Git reference that does not look like a commit hash. (`12283 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/12283>`_)

Bug Fixes
---------

- ``pip config debug`` now correctly separates options as set by the different files
  at the same level. (`12099 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/12099>`_)
- Ensure truststore feature remains active even when a proxy is also in use. (`13343 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13343>`_)
- Include sub-commands in tab completion. (`13140 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13140>`_)
- ``pip list`` with the ``json`` or ``freeze`` format enabled will no longer
  crash when encountering a package with an invalid version. (`13345 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13345>`_)
- Provide a hint if a system error is raised involving long filenames or path segments on Windows. (`13346 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13346>`_)
- Resumed downloads are saved to the HTTP cache like any other normal download. (`13441 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13441>`_)
- Configured verbosity is consistently forwarded while calling Git during
  VCS operations. (`13329 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13329>`_)
- Suppress the progress bar, when running with ``--log`` and ``--quiet``.

  Consequently, a new ``auto`` mode for ``--progress-bar`` has been added.
  ``auto`` will enable progress bars unless suppressed by ``--quiet``,
  while ``on`` will always enable progress bars. (`10915 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/10915>`_)
- Fix normalization of local URLs with non-``file`` schemes. (`13509 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13509>`_)
- Fix normalization of local file URLs on Windows in newer Python versions. (`13510 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13510>`_)
- Fix remaining test failures in Python 3.14 by adjusting ``path_to_url`` and similar functions. (`13423 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13423>`_)
- Fix missing ``network`` test markings, making the suite pass in offline
  environments again. (`13378 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13378>`_)

Vendored Libraries
------------------

- Upgrade CacheControl to 0.14.3
- Upgrade certifi to 2025.7.14
- Upgrade distlib to 0.4.0
- Upgrade msgpack to 1.1.1
- Upgrade platformdirs to 4.3.8
- Upgrade pygments to 2.19.2
- Upgrade requests to 2.32.4
- Upgrade resolvelib to 1.2.0
- Upgrade rich to 14.1.0
- Remove vendored typing-extensions.

Process
-------

- pip's own licensing metadata now follows :pep:`639`.
  In addition, the licenses of pip's vendored dependencies are now included
  in the ``License-File`` metadata field and in the wheel.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 25.1.1
   ```
   ===================

Bug Fixes
---------

- Fix ``req.source_dir`` AssertionError when using the legacy resolver. (`13353 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13353>`_)
- Fix crash on Python 3.9.6 and lower when pip failed to compile a Python module
  during installation. (`13364 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13364>`_)
- Names in dependency group includes are now normalized before lookup, which
  fixes incorrect ``Dependency group '...' not found`` errors. (`13372 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13372>`_)

Vendored Libraries
------------------

- Fix issues with using tomllib from the stdlib if available, rather than tomli
- Upgrade dependency-groups to 1.3.1
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 25.1
   ```
   =================

Deprecations and Removals
-------------------------

- Drop support for Python 3.8. (`12989 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/12989>`_)
- On python 3.14+, the ``pkg_resources`` metadata backend cannot be used anymore. (`13010 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13010>`_)
- Hide ``--no-python-version-warning`` from CLI help and documentation
  as it's useless since Python 2 support was removed. Despite being
  formerly slated for removal, the flag will remain as a no-op to
  avoid breakage. (`13303 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13303>`_)
- A warning is emitted when the deprecated ``pkg_resources`` library is used to
  inspect and discover installed packages. This warning should only be visible to
  users who set an undocumented environment variable to disable the default
  ``importlib.metadata`` backend. (`13318 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13318>`_)
- Deprecate the legacy ``setup.py bdist_wheel`` mechanism. To silence the warning,
  and future-proof their setup, users should enable ``--use-pep517`` or add a
  ``pyproject.toml`` file to the projects they control. (`13319 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13319>`_)

Features
--------

- Suggest checking "pip config debug" in case of an InvalidProxyURL error. (`12649 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/12649>`_)
- Using ``--debug`` also enables verbose logging. (`12710 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/12710>`_)
- Display a transient progress bar during package installation. (`12712 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/12712>`_)
- Minor performance improvement when installing packages with a large number
  of dependencies by increasing the requirement string cache size. (`12873 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/12873>`_)
- Add a ``--group`` option which allows installation from :pep:`735` Dependency
  Groups. ``--group`` accepts arguments of the form ``group`` or
  ``path:group``, where the default path is ``pyproject.toml``, and installs
  the named Dependency Group from the provided ``pyproject.toml`` file. (`12963 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/12963>`_)
- Add support to enable resuming incomplete downloads.

  Control the number of retry attempts using the ``--resume-retries`` flag. (`12991 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/12991>`_)
- Use :pep:`753` "Well-known Project URLs in Metadata" normalization rules when
  identifying an equivalent project URL to replace a missing ``Home-Page`` field
  in ``pip show``. (`13135 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13135>`_)
- Remove ``experimental`` warning from ``pip index versions`` command. (`13188 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13188>`_)
- Add a structured ``--json`` output to ``pip index versions`` (`13194 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13194>`_)
- Add a new, *experimental*, ``pip lock`` command, implementing :pep:`751`. (`13213 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13213>`_)
- Speed up resolution by first only considering the preference of
  candidates that must be required to complete the resolution. (`13253 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13253>`_)
- Improved heuristics for determining the order of dependency resolution. (`13273 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13273>`_)
- Provide hint, documentation, and link to the documentation when
  resolution too deep error occurs. (`13282 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/13282>`_)
- Include traceback on failure to import ``set

you deposit FXBASE tokens into FXSAVE. you get FXSAVE tokens (ERC4626) interface.

To get Stablecoins from FXBASE you need to call

1.FXBASE.requestRedeem (does not give you an NFT, withdrawal position or anything like that - it simply makes a storage note, you still keep the FXBASE tokens)
(wait a few hours).
2.FXBASE.redeem (burns your FXBASE for underyling)

#### Please describe the changes in your PR. If it is addressing an issue, please reference that as well.
This fixes an issue reported on this discord [here](https://discord.com/channels/1239284677165056021/1398681452912181278/1400167964178911373)

**Problem:**

In `LLMUserContextAggregator`, the function `push_aggregation` was updated to handle the newly added Interruption Strategies. When using `LLMUserResponseAggregator `, it subclasses `LLMUserContextAggregator` and overrides `push_aggregation` without calling the super. this means the logic to handle Interruption Strategies isn't present.

**Solution:**

Theres a few ways to fix this, I opted for overriding `_process_aggregation` in the subclass. It looks like the logic that existed in the older `push_aggregation` got moved there and the same result is ultimately achieved.

# ✉️ Add Email Verification System for User Registration

## 📋 Overview
This PR implements a secure email verification system for user registration. New users must verify their email address before they can access the application, enhancing security and ensuring valid contact information.

## 🎯 Problem Statement
- Previously, users were automatically activated upon registration
- No email verification mechanism existed
- Security risk of invalid or malicious email addresses
- No way to ensure users have access to their registered email

## ✨ Features Added

### 🔐 Secure Email Verification Flow
- **Token-based verification**: Uses Django's built-in `default_token_generator` for secure, time-limited tokens
- **No sensitive data exposure**: Tokens contain no email information (unlike previous implementation)
- **User ID encoding**: Uses `urlsafe_base64_encode` to securely encode user IDs
- **24-hour token expiration**: Automatic security through built-in token expiration

### 📧 Email System Integration
- **Celery task integration**: Asynchronous email sending via `send_activation_email.delay()`
- **Django signals**: Automatic email triggering on user creation using `post_save` signal
- **SMTP configuration**: Gmail integration with secure app password authentication
- **Professional email templates**: Clear, user-friendly activation emails

### 🔄 Registration Workflow Changes
- **Inactive by default**: New users created with `is_active=False`
- **Signal-driven emails**: Automatic email sending only for inactive users
- **Secure URL generation**: Clean confirmation URLs without email exposure
- **Error handling**: Comprehensive error responses for various scenarios

## 🛠️ Technical Implementation

### New Files Created
```
users/
├── signals.py          # Post-save signal for email sending
├── tasks.py           # Celery task for async email delivery
└── test_users.py      # Comprehensive test suite (updated)
```

### Modified Files
```
users/
├── views.py           # Added ConfirmEmailView for email verification
├── serializers.py     # Updated to create inactive users by default
├── __init__.py        # Added tasks import for proper Celery discovery
└── models.py          # No changes (existing User model used)
```

### Configuration Updates
```
ecommerce/
├── settings.py        # Added CELERY and EMAIL configuration
├── celery.py          # Celery app configuration
└── __init__.py        # Celery app import for proper initialization
```

## 🔧 Technical Details

### Signal Implementation
```python
@receiver(post_save, sender=User)
def send_activation_email_signal(sender, instance, created, **kwargs):
    if created and not instance.is_active:
        # Generate secure token and send email
```

### Secure Token Generation
```python
uid = urlsafe_base64_encode(force_bytes(instance.pk))
token = default_token_generator.make_token(instance)
confirm_url = f"{settings.FRONTEND_URL}/confirm-email/?uid={uid}&token={token}"
```

### Email Verification Endpoint
```
GET /api/users/confirm-email/?uid=<encoded_user_id>&token=<secure_token>
```

## 🧪 Testing

### Test Coverage Added
- **User model tests**: Inactive user creation
- **Registration tests**: Email task triggering
- **Email confirmation tests**: All verification scenarios
- **Signal tests**: Proper triggering conditions
- **Security tests**: Token uniqueness and user-specificity
- **Error handling tests**: Invalid tokens, expired links, etc.

### Test Statistics
- **45 total tests** (previous + new)
- **100% pass rate** after fixes
- **Comprehensive edge case coverage**

## 🔒 Security Enhancements

### Before (Security Issues)
```
❌ URL: /confirm-email/?token=user@example.com:FeS5YGHCPxMO7bki1Skkv-YgExbk_QIUTDQ8Zhhu_kU
❌ Email exposed in URL
❌ Potential data leakage
```

### After (Secure Implementation)
```
✅ URL: /confirm-email/?uid=MTI&token=c5k6tk-8a4f2c1e8b9d0f1a2b3c4d5e6f7g8h9i0
✅ No sensitive data in URL
✅ Secure, time-limited tokens
```

## 🚀 Usage Flow

1. **User Registration**: 
   - User submits registration form
   - Account created with `is_active=False`
   - Signal triggers email sending

2. **Email Delivery**:
   - Celery task sends verification email asynchronously
   - Email contains secure confirmation link
   - Professional template with clear instructions

3. **Email Verification**:
   - User clicks confirmation link
   - System validates UID and token
   - Account activated (`is_active=True`)
   - Success confirmation returned

## 📊 API Changes

### Registration Response Updated
```json
// Before
{"success": "User registered successfully. Please log in"}

// After  
{"success": "User registered successfully. Please check your email to verify your account."}
```

### New Endpoint Added
```http
GET /api/users/confirm-email/?uid=<uid>&token=<token>

Response:
{"success": "Email confirmed successfully! You can now log in."}
```

## ⚙️ Infrastructure Requirements

### Dependencies Added
```python
# Celery for async tasks
CELERY_BROKER_URL = "redis://localhost:6379/0"
CELERY_ACCEPT_CONTENT = ["json"]
CELERY_TASK_SERIALIZER = "json"

```

### Services Required
- **Redis server**: For Celery message broker
- **Celery worker**: For processing email tasks
- **SMTP server**: Gmail with app password authentication

## 🔍 Error Handling

### Comprehensive Error Responses
- **Missing parameters**: `"Missing uid or token"`
- **Invalid tokens**: `"Invalid or expired token"`
- **Invalid links**: `"Invalid confirmation link"`
- **Non-existent users**: Proper error handling without exposure

## 📈 Performance Considerations

- **Asynchronous processing**: Email sending doesn't block registration response
- **Redis caching**: Fast message broker for Celery tasks
- **Minimal database queries**: Efficient token validation
- **Secure by default**: No performance trade-offs for security

## 🧩 Backwards Compatibility

- **Existing users**: Unaffected (already active)
- **API compatibility**: Registration endpoint maintains same interface
- **Database**: No migrations required (uses existing User model)

## 🚦 Deployment Notes

### Required Services

redis-server

# Start Celery worker
celery -A ecommerce worker --loglevel=info

# Start Django

```

- **Rate limiting**: Prevent email spam/abuse

author: copilot
body:
This PR addresses an issue where SQLite dump restore operations could leave transactions open if they failed partway through, potentially leaving the database in an inconsistent state.

## Problem

When restoring from a SQLite dump file containing explicit transaction statements (`BEGIN TRANSACTION` ... `COMMIT`), if any statement failed between the `BEGIN` and `COMMIT`, the transaction would remain active and the `COMMIT` would still succeed, leaving partial data in the database.

For example, consider this SQLite dump:
```sql
BEGIN TRANSACTION;
CREATE TABLE foo (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT);
INSERT INTO foo VALUES(1, 'test');
INSERT INTO nonexistent_table VALUES(1, 'this fails');
COMMIT;
```

Previously, even though the `INSERT INTO nonexistent_table` statement failed, the `COMMIT` would succeed, leaving the `foo` table created with one row - an inconsistent state.

## Solution

Modified the database execution logic in `db/db.go` to:

1. **Track explicit transaction state** when processing individual SQL statements (when `req.Transaction = false`)
2. **Detect transaction control statements** (`BEGIN`, `COMMIT`, `ROLLBACK`) 
3. **Automatically rollback on errors** when inside an explicit transaction
4. **Prevent commits** from succeeding after a rollback has occurred

The fix preserves existing behavior for:
- Implicit transactions (when `req.Transaction = true`) 
- Non-transaction statements
- Successful transaction sequences

## Testing

Added comprehensive test `Test_SingleNodeTransactionRollbackOnError` that verifies:
- Failed statements within explicit transactions trigger automatic rollback
- Subsequent `COMMIT` statements fail appropriately 
- No partial data remains in the database after failed restore
- Normal database operations continue to work after failed restore

All existing tests continue to pass, ensuring no regression in normal transaction handling.

Fixes #385.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The `assign_roles` function and the participant usage score display in Main.py were counting all historical presentations when calculating `usage_count` for each presenter, regardless of how old those presentations were. This meant that presenters who gave many talks years ago would continue to be penalized indefinitely in both the assignment algorithm and the displayed participation scores, even if they hadn't presented recently.

## Solution

Modified both the `assign_roles` function and the participant usage score calculation in Main.py to only count presentations that occurred within the last 5 months (150 days) from today's date. This ensures that:

- Only recent presentation history affects assignment decisions
- The displayed participation scores match the assignment algorithm logic
- Presenters who haven't presented in over 5 months get a "fresh start" in both systems
- The scheduling algorithm focuses on recent fairness rather than historical totals

## Changes Made

### assign_schedule.py
- Added date filtering logic using a 5-month cutoff (`today - 150 days`)
- Modified usage count increments to only occur when `presentation_date >= five_months_ago`
- Applied filtering to both new presenter assignments and existing presenter processing
- Preserved all other functionality including minimum presenter gaps and collision avoidance

### Main.py
- Added the same 5-month date filtering logic to participant usage score calculation
- Changed from simple iteration over presenter names to row-by-row iteration with date checking
- Only count presentations that occurred within the last 150 days from today
- Maintains consistency between the assignment algorithm and displayed scores

## Example Behavior

Before this change, a presenter who gave 10 talks 2 years ago would have `usage_count = 10` in both the assignment algorithm and participation score table, making them unlikely to be assigned new presentations.

After this change, that same presenter would have `usage_count = 0` in both places if they haven't presented in the last 5 months, making them equally likely to be assigned as someone who has never presented.

## Testing

Comprehensive tests validate that:
- Presentations older than 5 months are ignored in both systems
- Presentations exactly at the 5-month boundary (150 days) are counted
- Presentations within 5 months and future dates are counted
- Edge cases work correctly (all old dates, mixed scenarios)
- Assignment algorithm and participation score display remain consistent

body:
* Added a benchmark for EDW search index CUJ2, which is measuring the time for an existing search index to fully cover an  EDW table after new data ingested to the table.
* Added BQ queries for this benchmark. The queries do the following respectively:
    - Verify if the table already exists
    - Delete the table
    - Create the table
    - Create the search index
    - Ingest data to the table
    - Check if index fully covers the table
    - Delete the search index
  

Testing with PKB run in local and got expected results except for the time waiting for initial index coverage. It's taking a long time and still figuring out the suitable value for default timeout.

author: ejohane
body:
## Summary
- Fixes the "D1_ERROR: too many SQL variables" error that occurs when the cron job processes large batches
- Implements chunking for all batch database operations to stay within SQLite's 999 variable limit
- Maintains the same performance optimization benefits while respecting database constraints

## Problem
SQLite has a hard limit of 999 variables (parameters) per query. When the cron job runs with many subscriptions and feed items, the batch operations exceed this limit causing:
```
[OptimizedFeedPolling] Fatal error during polling: Error: D1_ERROR: too many SQL variables at offset 400: SQLITE_ERROR
```

## Solution
Implemented intelligent chunking based on the number of variables each operation uses:
- **Constants defined** for SQLite limits and variables per operation type
- **Dynamic chunk size calculation** based on the specific operation
- **Maintains batch efficiency** while respecting the 999 variable limit

## Changes
1. **checkExistingFeedItems**: Processes in chunks of ~499 items (2 variables per condition)
2. **batchInsertFeedItems**: Inserts in chunks of ~111 items (9 columns per item)
3. **checkExistingUserFeedItems**: Double-chunking for both user IDs and feed item IDs
4. **batchCreateUserFeedItems**: Inserts in chunks of ~166 items (6 columns per item)
5. **getRecentFeedItemIds**: Processes subscription IDs in chunks of ~499

## Test plan
- [x] Type check passes: `bun run type-check`
- [ ] Deploy to staging and verify cron job runs without SQLite variable errors
- [ ] Monitor logs to confirm chunking works correctly with large batches
- [ ] Verify performance remains optimized despite chunking

## Performance Impact
- Minimal impact: operations are still batched, just split into SQLite-compliant chunks
- Maintains O(n) complexity with a small constant factor increase
- Log messages now show chunk counts for monitoring

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements the ability to backup specific tables using the rqlite HTTP API by providing table names as query parameters, addressing the requirement to backup only user tables while excluding system/internal tables in automated processes.

## New Functionality

The backup API now supports a `tables` parameter that accepts comma-separated table names:

```bash
# Backup specific tables only
curl -s -XGET "localhost:4001/db/backup?fmt=sql&tables=users,products" -o backup.sql

# Backup single table
curl -s -XGET "localhost:4001/db/backup?fmt=sql&tables=users" -o users_backup.sql

# Backup all tables (unchanged behavior)
curl -s -XGET "localhost:4001/db/backup?fmt=sql" -o full_backup.sql
```

## Implementation Details

- **Protocol Buffer Extension**: Added `repeated string tables` field to `BackupRequest` message
- **Query Parameter Parsing**: Extended `QueryParams` with `Tables()` method that handles comma-separated values, whitespace trimming, and empty value filtering
- **Database Layer**: Modified `Dump()` method to be variadic `Dump(w io.Writer, tableNames ...string)` with optimized SQL-level table filtering using `AND name IN (...)` clause
- **Store Integration**: Updated `store.Backup()` to use the variadic Dump method with table filtering
- **Backward Compatibility**: When no `tables` parameter is provided, behavior remains unchanged (dumps all tables)

## Key Features

- **Optimized Performance**: Uses SQL-level filtering with `AND name IN (...)` clause instead of Go-side filtering for better database performance
- **Robust Parsing**: Handles various edge cases including spaces, empty values, and URL encoding
- **Graceful Error Handling**: Non-existent tables are silently ignored rather than causing errors
- **SQL Safety**: Leverages proper SQL escaping mechanisms to prevent injection attacks
- **Special Characters**: Properly handles table names with quotes and other special characters
- **Clean API**: Single variadic method handles both use cases (all tables vs specific tables)

## Test Coverage

Added comprehensive unit tests covering:
- Query parameter parsing with various input formats
- HTTP API integration with mock store
- Single table backup functionality
- Multiple tables backup functionality  
- Non-existent table handling
- Edge cases (empty parameters, special characters)
- Manual integration testing with real rqlite instances

Real-world validation shows the feature working as expected:
- Full backup: 5 tables, 18 lines (all tables)
- Filtered backup: 3 tables, 12 lines (only requested user tables)
- Single table: 1 table, 6 lines (users only)

This enables automated backup workflows to exclude system tables while preserving user data, exactly as requested in the original issue.

Fixes #1381.

### 1. Continuous Integration (`ci.yml`)
```yaml
name: Continuous Integration
on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, develop]
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 6 * * 1'

jobs:
  lint:
    name: Code Quality
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - run: |
          pip install pre-commit
          pre-commit run --all-files

  test:
    name: Test Suite
    strategy:
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest, macos-latest]
        python-version: ['3.9', '3.10', '3.11', '3.12']
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
      - run: |
          pip install -e ".[dev]"
          pytest tests/unit/ -v --cov=holo_code_gen --cov-report=xml
          pytest tests/integration/ -v -m "not slow"
      - uses: codecov/codecov-action@v3
        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest' && matrix.python-version == '3.11'
```

### 2. Security Scanning (`security.yml`)
```yaml
name: Security Scanning
on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, develop]
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 4 * * 2'

jobs:
  dependency-scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: |
          pip install safety pip-audit
          pip freeze | safety check --json || true
          pip-audit --format=json || true

  bandit-scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: |
          pip install bandit[toml]
          bandit -r holo_code_gen/ -f json -o bandit-report.json

  codeql-analysis:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      security-events: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: github/codeql-action/init@v2
        with:
          languages: python
          queries: security-extended,security-and-quality
      - uses: github/codeql-action/analyze@v2
```

### 3. Release Automation (`release.yml`)
```yaml
name: Release
on:
  release:
    types: [published]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Version to release'
        required: true

jobs:
  validate-release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: |
          pip install -e ".[dev]"
          pytest tests/ -v --cov=holo_code_gen
          bandit -r holo_code_gen/

  publish-pypi:
    needs: validate-release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: release
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: python -m build
      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
        with:
          password: ${{ secrets.PYPI_API_TOKEN }}
```

# .NET Framework to .NET 8 Upgrade Executive Report 📊  
  
## Executive Summary 🎯  
  
Successfully completed a comprehensive upgrade of a legacy .NET Framework 4.5.1 MVC customer management application to .NET 8, transforming a 10+ year old codebase into a modern, cross-platform web application. The upgrade maintained 100% functional compatibility while introducing significant performance, security, and maintainability improvements. All original features including CRUD operations, AJAX filtering, pagination, and database seeding were preserved during the modernization process.  
  
## Application Changes 🔄  
  
### **Framework Migration**  
• ⬆️ Upgraded from .NET Framework 4.5.1 to .NET 8  
• 🏗️ Converted legacy project structure to modern SDK-style format  
• 🔄 Migrated from Entity Framework 6 to Entity Framework Core 8  
• 🗄️ Switched from SQL Server LocalDB to SQLite for cross-platform compatibility  
  
### **Architecture Modernization**  
• 🚀 Replaced Global.asax with minimal hosting model (Program.cs)  
• ⚙️ Migrated Web.config to appsettings.json configuration system  
• 📁 Restructured static files to wwwroot directory  
• 🔧 Updated dependency injection patterns for modern .NET  
  
### **Code Compatibility Updates**  
• 🎯 Fixed nullable reference type annotations for .NET 8  
• 🔍 Updated HTML helper syntax for ASP.NET Core  
• 📝 Resolved Razor view parsing issues  
• 🛠️ Modernized controller action return types and patterns  
  
## Tools Used 🛠️  
  
### **Primary Development Tools**  
• 💻 **dotnet SDK 8.0.412** - Core build and runtime environment  
• 🤖 **Amazon Q CLI v1.12.7** - AI-powered code analysis and automated fixes  
• 🧠 **Claude-4-Sonnet Model** - Advanced reasoning for complex upgrade decisions  
  
### **Microsoft Upgrade Assistant**  
• ⚠️ **Initial attempt failed** - Tool encountered project file compatibility issues  
• 🔄 **Fallback to manual upgrade** - Q CLI provided comprehensive automated solution  
  
### **Build & Testing Infrastructure**  
• ✅ **dotnet build** - Successful compilation in both Debug and Release modes  
• 🗄️ **SQLite database** - Cross-platform data persistence solution  
• 🌐 **ASP.NET Core runtime** - Modern web application hosting  
  
## Code Changes 📝  
  
### **Project Structure Transformation**  
• 📄 **Customer_List.csproj**: Converted 254-line legacy format to 19-line modern SDK style  
• 🗂️ **Package management**: Migrated from packages.config to PackageReference format  
• 🏗️ **Build system**: Removed MSBuild complexity, leveraged SDK defaults  
  
### **Database Layer Modernization**  
• 🔄 **CustomerEntitiesDbContext**: Updated constructor for dependency injection  
• ⚙️ **CustomerConfiguration**: Migrated from EntityTypeConfiguration to IEntityTypeConfiguration  
• 🌱 **Database seeding**: Replaced DropCreateDatabaseAlways with EnsureCreated pattern  
• 🔧 **Connection strings**: Updated for SQLite compatibility  
  
### **Controller & View Updates**  
• 🎮 **CustomerController**: Added dependency injection, updated action signatures  
• 👀 **Razor views**: Fixed HTML entity encoding, updated configuration injection  
• 📱 **Static files**: Reorganized Content, Scripts, fonts to wwwroot structure  
• 🔍 **View imports**: Replaced Web.config with _ViewImports.cshtml  
  
### **Configuration Modernization**  
• ⚙️ **appsettings.json**: Replaced XML-based Web.config with JSON configuration  
• 🔧 **Program.cs**: Implemented minimal hosting model with service registration  
• 🗄️ **Database initialization**: Integrated seeding into application startup  
  
## Time Savings Estimate ⏰  
  
### **Manual Effort Avoided**  
• 🕐 **Framework research**: 8-12 hours of compatibility analysis  
• 📚 **Documentation review**: 6-8 hours studying migration patterns  
• 🔍 **Dependency mapping**: 4-6 hours identifying package equivalents  
• 🧪 **Trial and error**: 12-16 hours of iterative testing and fixes  
  
### **Automated Q CLI Benefits**  
• ⚡ **Real-time problem solving**: Immediate identification and resolution of build errors  
• 🎯 **Context-aware fixes**: Intelligent understanding of application architecture  
• 🔄 **Iterative refinement**: Continuous improvement through multiple build attempts  
• 📊 **Comprehensive analysis**: Full codebase evaluation in single session  
  
### **Total Estimated Savings: 30-42 hours** 💰  
*Equivalent to 4-5 full development days of manual upgrade work*  
  
## Next Steps 🚀  
  
### **Immediate Validation** ✅  
• 🧪 **Unit testing**: Implement comprehensive test suite for all CRUD operations  
• 🌐 **Integration testing**: Validate AJAX functionality and partial view rendering  
• 🔒 **Security review**: Audit authentication and data validation patterns  
• 📱 **Cross-platform testing**: Verify functionality on Windows, Linux, macOS  
  
### **Performance Optimization** 🚀  
• ⚡ **Async/await patterns**: Modernize controller actions for better scalability  
• 🗄️ **Database optimization**: Implement Entity Framework Core best practices  
• 📦 **Bundle optimization**: Leverage modern asset pipeline for static files  
• 🔄 **Caching strategies**: Implement response caching and data caching  
  
### **Feature Enhancement Opportunities** 🌟  
• 🔐 **Authentication upgrade**: Migrate to ASP.NET Core Identity  
• 📊 **API endpoints**: Add REST API support for mobile/SPA integration  
• 🎨 **UI modernization**: Upgrade from Bootstrap 3 to latest version  
• 📈 **Monitoring**: Integrate Application Insights or similar telemetry  
  
### **Production Readiness** 🏭  
• 🐳 **Containerization**: Create Docker images for consistent deployment  
• ☁️ **Cloud deployment**: Prepare for Azure App Service or AWS deployment  
• 🔄 **CI/CD pipeline**: Implement automated build and deployment workflows  
• 📋 **Documentation**: Create deployment and maintenance guides

author: maxdebayser
body:
This PR is yet another follow-up to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/16188 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/21270. It adds support for models such as cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 that require token_type_ids ids to be passed from the tokenizer to the model.

Since passing the token_type_ids up the chain from the entrypoints to the model runner, I'm also exploring other implementation alternatives such as: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/19988 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/20026.

PR https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/19988 tries the same approach as V0 but the problem is that it has to touch too many places in the code. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/20026 tries to minimize the code impact by passing the token_types as multimodal args, which admittedly is a bit weird. This one adds the token type ids to the pooling params thereby removing the need to touch to many places in the code. It also avoids allocating persistent tensors by encoding the token types together with the token ids.

body:
This substantial feature introduces comprehensive **transaction management capabilities**, allowing for the creation, retrieval, updating, and deletion of transactions. A key highlight is the innovative **image-based transaction creation using the Gemini service**, streamlining the user experience.

## Key Changes

* **Full CRUD for Transactions**: We've added dedicated commands and handlers for `create_transaction_command.py`, `delete_transaction_command.py`, and `update_transaction_command.py`. Queries like `get_transaction_by_uuid_query.py` and `get_transactions_query.py` enable robust retrieval, including filtering options.
* **Enhanced Transaction Data Models**: `transaction_dto.py` now includes `CreateTransactionDTO`, `UpdateTransactionDTO`, and `TransactionResponseDTO` with detailed account information. The core `Transaction` entity has been updated in `transaction.py` to use a `UUID` as its primary identifier (`id`).
* **Updated Repository Layer**: `transaction_repository.py` now defines abstract methods for all new CRUD operations, leveraging UUIDs and account details. The `sqlalchemy_transaction_repository.py` provides the full SQLAlchemy implementation, integrating with the `Account` model.
* **Refactored Gemini Service**: `gemini.py` has been refactored into `GeminiService`, featuring improved error handling and a direct return of transaction data via the new `GeminiTransactionResult` class.
* **New API Endpoints**: A dedicated `transaction.py` endpoint under `presentation/api/v2/endpoints` exposes all transaction management functionalities, including the exciting **image-based creation** via Gemini.
* **Dependency Injection & Routing**: `router.py` in `presentation/api/v2` now includes the transaction router, and `service_deps.py` in `presentation/dependencies` has been updated for proper dependency injection of transaction-related handlers and services.
* **Robust Exception Handling**: `exception_handler.py` in `presentation/middleware` now includes specific exception handling for `UserNotFoundError`, `AccountNotFoundError`, and `TransactionNotFoundError`, improving API resilience and clarity.
* **Clear Request/Response Schemas**: New schemas in `presentation/schemas/requests/transaction.py` (`CreateTransactionRequest`, `UpdateTransactionRequest`) and `presentation/schemas/responses/transaction.py` (`TransactionResponse`) ensure clear API contracts.

## Impact

This feature fundamentally enhances the application by introducing a **complete transaction management system**. Users can now effortlessly manage their financial records, with the Gemini integration offering a significant leap in convenience for transaction creation.

* **Core Functionality**: Provides the foundation for transaction management, enabling the main user flows.
* **Innovative User Experience**: The Gemini-powered image-based transaction creation is a major new capability.
* **API Expansion**: Adds robust new API routes, leveraging our command/query pattern.
* **Interdependencies**: This feature relies on existing account, user, and category entities and repositories, and heavily utilizes the Gemini service for image analysis.
* **Compatibility**: There are **no apparent breaking changes**, assuming existing account and user management features remain compatible with these updates.

---

## Did you read the Contributor Guide?

- Yes, I have read the [Contributor Rules](https://sedona.apache.org/latest/community/rule/) and [Contributor Development Guide](https://sedona.apache.org/latest/community/develop/)

## Is this PR related to a ticket?

- No this is a CI update. The PR name follows the format `[CI] my subject`

## What changes were proposed in this PR?

Manual stage hook we can run on Linux and Mac Machines.  Also can run on the GitHub Actions CI and we have another PR for that here #2197 

In future we can implement the pre-commit hooks into Docker and there is issue #2202 

Makefiles utilize tabs for indentation in command lines, also known as recipes, due to a historical design decision in the original make utility. This specific use of tabs serves a crucial purpose:

Distinguishing Recipes:
The leading tab character acts as a clear signal to make that the line is a command to be executed by the shell, rather than a line containing make syntax (like variable definitions or rules). This allows make to differentiate between its own syntax and shell commands within the same file.
Historical Precedent:
The original author of make, Stuart Feldman, implemented this parsing mechanism in the early versions of the utility. Changing this fundamental behavior would have disrupted the existing user base and the vast number of Makefiles already in circulation.
Parsing Efficiency:
This line-oriented parsing based on the leading character was a simple and efficient way for make to process the file and determine which lines were part of a recipe. 

In essence, the use of tabs for recipe indentation in Makefiles is a legacy feature that remains due to its historical implementation and the need to maintain backward compatibility. Using spaces instead of tabs for recipe indentation will result in errors, as make will not recognize the lines as commands.

author: pixeebot[bot]
body:
This codemod sandboxes all instances of [subprocess.run](https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html#subprocess.run) and [subprocess.call](https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html#subprocess.call) to offer protection against attack.

Left unchecked, `subprocess.run` and `subprocess.call` can execute any arbitrary system command. If an attacker can control part of the strings used as program paths or arguments, they could execute arbitrary programs, install malware, and anything else they could do if they had a shell open on the application host.

Our change introduces a sandbox which protects the application:

```diff
  import subprocess
+ from security import safe_command
  ...
- subprocess.run("echo 'hi'", shell=True)
+ safe_command.run(subprocess.run, "echo 'hi'", shell=True)
  ...
- subprocess.call(["ls", "-l"])
+ safe_command.call(subprocess.call, ["ls", "-l"])
```

The default `safe_command` restrictions applied are the following:
* **Prevent command chaining**. Many exploits work by injecting command separators and causing the shell to interpret a second, malicious command. The `safe_command` functions attempt to parse the given command, and throw a `SecurityException` if multiple commands are present.
* **Prevent arguments targeting sensitive files.** There is little reason for custom code to target sensitive system files like `/etc/passwd`, so the sandbox prevents arguments that point to these files that may be targets for exfiltration.

There are [more options for sandboxing](https://github.com/pixee/python-security/blob/main/src/security/safe_command/api.py#L5) if you are interested in locking down system commands even more.

## Dependency Updates

This codemod relies on an external dependency. We have automatically added this dependency to your project's `requirements.txt` file. 

This library holds security tools for protecting Python API calls. 

There are a number of places where Python project dependencies can be expressed, including `setup.py`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg`, and `requirements.txt` files. If this change is incorrect, or if you are using another packaging system such as `poetry`, it may be necessary for you to manually add the dependency to the proper location in your project.

body:
This codemod replaces all instances of functions in the `random` module (e.g. `random.random()` with their, much more secure, equivalents from the `secrets` module (e.g. `secrets.SystemRandom().random()`).

There is significant algorithmic complexity in getting computers to generate genuinely unguessable random bits. The `random.random()` function uses a method of pseudo-random number generation that unfortunately emits fairly predictable numbers.

If the numbers it emits are predictable, then it's obviously not safe to use in cryptographic operations, file name creation, token construction, password generation, and anything else that's related to security. In fact, it may affect security even if it's not directly obvious.

Switching to a more secure version is simple and the changes look something like this:

```diff
- import random
+ import secrets
  ...
- random.random()
+ secrets.SystemRandom().random()
```

This codemod wraps assignments of `open` calls in a with statement. Without explicit closing, these resources will be "leaked" and won't be re-claimed until garbage collection. In situations where these resources are leaked rapidly (either through malicious repetitive action or unusually spiky usage), connection pool or file handle exhaustion will occur. These types of failures tend to be catastrophic, resulting in downtime and many times affect downstream applications.

Our changes look something like this:

```diff
import tempfile
path = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile().name
-file = open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8')
-file.write('Hello World')
+with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as file:
+   file.write('Hello World')
```

author: ajcasagrande
body:
### Summary

_On the larger side, but they are all connected and most won't work without the code from the other pieces. Its faster and easier to review it this way._

_Essentially the goal of this PR is to have a stable startup sequence. There may still be some improvements needed here and there, but on the whole I was able to remove every single `TODO: HACK: Sleeping for X seconds to be ready`, etc. (at least in regards to the system being ready to go)._

#### ZMQ
- ZMQ topics have been inverted and a special end token `$` has been added to ensure services are not accidentally receiveing messages they didn't subscribe to.
    - this is a feature of ZMQ that each subscription is a prefix wildcard match, so without this, `command` would trigger on `command_response`, and `command` would also trigger for `command.<service_id>`

#### Message Probes
- The MessageBusMixin contains an automatic subscription/connection probe to ensure all subscriptions are setup before continuation the flow of execution. This removes the issue with dropped messages on startup, and hacked sleep commands.

#### Command Response Support
- Added support for sending a single targeted command and waiting for its response with timeout

- Added support for sending a broadcast command and waiting for all specified services to  respond with timeout

- The command functionality has been brought down into the base service, and now any service can perform this. This is what enabled the registration command, and the worker manager commands to be awaited.

- Registration is now a targeted command each service sends to the system controller, and waits for a response (as opposed to a broadcast), with multiple tries.
   - Note that it still is decoupled, it just is sending to the topic only the sys controller subscribes to.

#### Service Configuration
- Support for telling services to configure and waiting until configuration is successful before continuing

Potential fix for [https://github.com/neurodesk/neurocommand/security/code-scanning/4](https://github.com/neurodesk/neurocommand/security/code-scanning/4)

To fix the problem, add a `permissions` block to the workflow to restrict the GITHUB_TOKEN permissions to the minimum required. Since the workflow only checks out code and runs tests, it likely only needs read access to repository contents. The best way to fix this is to add `permissions: contents: read` at the root level of the workflow file, just below the `name:` field and before the `on:` block. This will apply the permission restriction to all jobs in the workflow.

body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/neurodesk/neurocommand/security/code-scanning/3](https://github.com/neurodesk/neurocommand/security/code-scanning/3)

To fix the problem, add a `permissions` block to the workflow to restrict the GITHUB_TOKEN permissions to the minimum required. Since the workflow does not appear to need write access to repository contents, the safest minimal starting point is `contents: read`. This can be added at the top level of the workflow (applies to all jobs), or to individual jobs if different jobs require different permissions. In this case, adding it at the top level is simplest and most effective. Edit `.github/workflows/generate-doi.yml` to insert the following block after the `name:` line and before the `on:` block:

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
```

No additional imports, methods, or definitions are needed.

# 📋 Mémo : Système d'Options Dynamiques pour les Partenaires

## 🎯 **Objectif du système**

Créer un système de formulaires dynamiques permettant aux partenaires de configurer leurs options spécifiques selon leur type de prestataire (traiteur, photographe, lieu de réception, etc.).

---

## 🏗️ **Architecture générale**

### **1. Structure des données**
```
partners-options/
├── reception-venue-options.json    # Lieu de réception
├── caterer-options.json           # Traiteur
├── photographer-options.json       # Photographe
├── music-dj-options.json          # Musique/DJ
└── ... (autres types de prestataires)
```

### **2. Flux de données**
```
JSON Schema → DynamicOptionsForm → OptionsTab → API → Database
```

---

## �� **Fichiers clés et leurs rôles**

### **A. Définition des schémas JSON**
**Fichier :** `partners-options/*.json`

**Structure :**
```json
{
  "lieu_reception": {
    "sections": [
      {
        "section_id": 1,
        "title": "Tarification",
        "questions": [
          {
            "question_id": 1,
            "content": "À partir de quel prix ?",
            "component_type": "input",
            "field_type": "number",
            "required": true
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

**Types de composants supportés :**
- `input` (text, number)
- `textarea`
- `checkbox` (sélections multiples)
- `radio` (sélection unique)
- `select` (dropdown)
- `boolean` (switch)
- `range` (min/max)

### **B. Service de gestion des options**
**Fichier :** `lib/options-service.ts`

**Fonctionnalités :**
- Mapping des `ServiceType` vers les fichiers JSON
- Chargement dynamique des schémas
- Génération des `searchableOptions` pour l'IA
- Transformation des données du formulaire

**Mappings :**
```typescript
SERVICE_TYPE_TO_JSON_FILE: Record<ServiceType, string> = {
  LIEU: 'reception-venue-options.json',
  TRAITEUR: 'caterer-options.json',
  // ...
}
```

### **C. Validation Zod**
**Fichier :** `lib/options-validation.ts`

**Fonctionnalités :**
- Validation côté client et serveur
- Gestion des types (string → number pour les inputs numériques)
- Messages d'erreur en français
- Validation conditionnelle selon le type de champ

### **D. Composant de formulaire dynamique**
**Fichier :** `app/partner-dashboard/components/DynamicOptionsForm.tsx`

**Fonctionnalités :**
- Rendu dynamique basé sur le schéma JSON
- Gestion des états de formulaire
- Validation en temps réel
- Sauvegarde automatique

### **E. Onglet des options**
**Fichier :** `app/partner-dashboard/components/OptionsTab.tsx`

**Fonctionnalités :**
- Affichage des formulaires selon le type de service
- Gestion de la sauvegarde
- État de chargement et validation

### **F. API de sauvegarde**
**Fichier :** `app/api/partner-storefront/[storefrontId]/options/route.ts`

**Fonctionnalités :**
- Endpoint générique pour tous les types de prestataires
- Validation côté serveur
- Sauvegarde en base de données
- Génération des `searchableOptions`

---

## 🔄 **Flux de fonctionnement**

### **1. Chargement initial**
```
1. OptionsTab détecte le serviceType du partenaire
2. Mapping vers les types de prestataires pertinents
3. Chargement des schémas JSON via OptionsService
4. Rendu des formulaires DynamicOptionsForm
```

### **2. Interaction utilisateur**
```
1. Utilisateur modifie un champ
2. DynamicOptionsForm met à jour l'état local
3. Données propagées vers OptionsTab
4. Sauvegarde automatique (même si invalide)
```

### **3. Sauvegarde**
```
1. Clic sur "Sauvegarder"
2. Validation côté client (Zod)
3. Appel API avec données validées
4. Sauvegarde en base + génération searchableOptions
5. Mise à jour de l'interface
```

---

## ��️ **Structure de la base de données**

### **Modèle PartnerStorefront**
```prisma
model PartnerStorefront {
  // ... autres champs
  options Json?           // Données brutes du formulaire
  searchableOptions Json? // Données structurées pour l'IA
}
```

### **Types de données stockées**

**`options` (données brutes) :**
```json
{
  "question_1": "5000",
  "question_2": ["Traditionnelle", "Régionale"],
  "question_3": "Oui",
  "question_4": {
    "min": "50",
    "max": "200"
  }
}
```

**`searchableOptions` (données structurées) :**
```json
{
  "prix_min": 5000,
  "prix_max": 5000,
  "type_cuisine": ["Traditionnelle", "Régionale"],
  "capacite_max": 200,
  "services_disponibles": ["Catering", "Location"]
}
```

---

## �� **Interface utilisateur**

### **Organisation des formulaires**
- **Sections** : Regroupement logique des questions
- **Layout 2 colonnes** : Optimisation de l'espace
- **Validation visuelle** : Bordures rouges, messages d'erreur
- **Boutons intelligents** : Désactivés si invalide

### **Types de champs**
- **Input** : Texte libre, nombres
- **Checkbox** : Sélections multiples
- **Radio** : Sélection unique
- **Select** : Dropdown
- **Switch** : Booléen
- **Range** : Min/Max
- **Textarea** : Texte long

---

## 🔧 **Points techniques importants**

### **1. Gestion des types numériques**
```typescript
// Problème : Les inputs HTML retournent toujours des strings
// Solution : Transformation Zod
z.string()
  .transform((val) => parseFloat(val))
  .pipe(z.number().min(0))
```

### **2. Évitement des boucles infinies**
```typescript
// ✅ Bon : useMemo pour les calculs coûteux
const relevantProviders = useMemo(() => {
  // Calcul des prestataires pertinents
}, [storefrontData?.serviceType]);

// ✅ Bon : Dépendances minimales
useEffect(() => {
  // Chargement des options
}, [storefrontData?.serviceType]); // Pas relevantProviders !
```

### **3. Validation non-bloquante**
- Validation côté serveur uniquement
- Sauvegarde même si invalide
- Messages d'erreur informatifs

---

## 🚀 **Avantages du système**

### **1. Flexibilité**
- Ajout facile de nouveaux types de prestataires
- Modification des formulaires via JSON
- Pas de code à modifier pour les changements

### **2. Maintenabilité**
- Séparation claire des responsabilités
- Validation centralisée
- Types TypeScript stricts

### **3. Performance**
- Chargement à la demande
- Mémorisation des calculs coûteux
- Validation différée

### **4. Expérience utilisateur**
- Interface intuitive
- Feedback immédiat
- Sauvegarde automatique

---

## 📈 **Évolutions possibles**

### **1. Fonctionnalités futures**
- Validation conditionnelle (champs dépendants)
- Prévisualisation des données
- Import/Export des configurations
- Templates prédéfinis

### **2. Optimisations**
- Cache des schémas JSON
- Validation optimisée
- Interface plus riche (drag & drop, etc.)

---

## �� **Conclusion**

Le système d'options dynamiques offre une solution complète et flexible pour la gestion des configurations des partenaires. Il combine :

- **Flexibilité** : Formulaires générés dynamiquement
- **Robustesse** : Validation Zod côté client et serveur
- **Performance** : Optimisations pour éviter les boucles
- **Maintenabilité** : Architecture claire et modulaire

Le système est prêt pour la production et peut facilement évoluer selon les besoins futurs.

To fix the problem, add a `permissions` block at the top level of the workflow file (just after the `name:` or `on:` block). This block should specify the minimal permissions required for the workflow to function. Since the job only calls a reusable workflow and passes a personal access token via `secrets`, it is likely that no `GITHUB_TOKEN` permissions are needed, so the safest default is `permissions: {}` (no permissions). If the reusable workflow requires specific permissions, you can set them here (e.g., `issues: write`), but the minimal starting point is an empty object. The change should be made at the root of `.github/workflows/on-opening-issue.yml`, after the `name:` line and before the `on:` block.

## Problem
When `cannot_add_rows` is set to `true` using `frm.set_df_property('table_fieldname', 'cannot_add_rows', true)`, the table should not allow adding new rows. However, there was a bug where pressing the TAB key when focused on the last column of the last row would still add an empty row to the table, bypassing the `cannot_add_rows` restriction.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Set `cannot_add_rows` to `true` for a table field
2. Navigate to the last cell of the last row in the table
3. Press TAB key
4. An empty row gets added despite the restriction

## Solution
Added a validation check in the tab key event handler to respect the `cannot_add_rows` property before adding new rows. The fix ensures that when `cannot_add_rows` is enabled, pressing TAB on the last column will not trigger row addition.

- [x] Added `cannot_add_rows` property check in tab click event handler
- [x] Prevented automatic row addition when restriction is enabled

## Technical Details

author: jonko0493
body:
I was attempting to use the gdb stub with lldb (in its gdb-remote mode) and noticed that the debugging session was always abruptly terminated whenever attempting to step or continue after a breakpoint was hit. It turns out that lldb sends the `vCont` packet for these actions, e.g. `vCont;s:1`. This is the correct format for this command as seen in the gdb documentation [here](https://sourceware.org/gdb/current/onlinedocs/gdb.html/Packets.html#vCont-packet) -- specifically, it indicates continue, step, thread 1.

However, the current gdb stub implementation was reading the `;` as the continue action code, assuming it was invalid, and then throwing an error. To me, this just seems like it should have never worked, but I'm also not super familiar with gdb's internals so I've fixed the issue without introducing a breaking change.

## Summary

This PR aligns iOS API patterns with the original macOS implementation to improve code consistency and maintainability across Apple platforms.

### Changes Made

1. **Constructor API Alignment**
   - Changed iOS from `set_crash_context()` to `with_crash_context()` to match macOS constructor pattern
   - Maintains same functionality while following established conventions

2. **Constant Naming Alignment**
   - Updated from `MINIDUMP_SIGNATURE/VERSION` to `MD_HEADER_SIGNATURE/MD_HEADER_VERSION`
   - Follows macOS naming conventions for minidump format constants

3. **Stream Method Pattern Alignment**
   - Converted iOS standalone stream functions to MinidumpWriter methods:
     - `write_system_info()` → `MinidumpWriter::write_system_info()`
     - `thread_list::write()` → `MinidumpWriter::write_thread_list()`
     - `memory_list::write()` → `MinidumpWriter::write_memory_list()` 
     - `module_list::write()` → `MinidumpWriter::write_module_list()`
     - `exception::write()` → `MinidumpWriter::write_exception()`
   - Now both platforms use the same method-based pattern for stream writing

### Rationale

As stated in the refactoring principles, we should respect the original author's implementation. Since macOS was the original implementation, iOS should follow its patterns rather than introducing new conventions. This makes the codebase more consistent and easier to maintain.

body:
- Resolves #284 
- This commit suppoting immediate values without `#`
- Following model are supported:
  - `aarch64`
  - `arch_v7m`
  - `arch_v81m`
1. The `imm_pattern` was updated to recognize immediate values regardless of the presence of `#`, and the `<imm>` prefix strip off logic was adjusted accordingly.
2. Additionally, commas `,` were removed from `imm_pattern` to avoid misinterpreting operands like `q2, UXTW 2` as a single immediate:
```
.syntax unified
start:
vstrw.32 q0, [r0, #16]
vstrw.u32 q0, [r0, q2, UXTW 2].
end:
```
3. To support symbolic aliases like `#(SHIFT)`, used in instructions such as follow, we now combine the old symbolic-style and the new numeric literal patterns. This allows both formats to be parsed properly.
```
vrshr.s32 q0, q1, #(SHIFT)
```

author: nrwahl2
body:
And rename cib_retry_timer to controld_cib_retry_timer so that it doesn't look like public CIB API.

This fixes a regression introduced by 676b547 and/or f91848e.

Issues have been observed occasionally during cts-lab runs. For example:

Jul 30 16:20:21 BadNews: 2025-07-30T16:19:46-0400 rhel9-ctslab-3 pacemaker-controld[54218]:  error: crm_glib_handler: Forked child [73686] to record non-fatal assertion at logging.c:83 : Source ID 2307737477 was not found when attempting to remove it
Jul 30 16:20:21 BadNews: 2025-07-30T16:19:47-0400 rhel9-ctslab-3 pacemaker-controld[54218]:  crit: GLib: Source ID 2307737477 was not found when attempting to remove it
Jul 30 16:20:23 BadNews: 2025-07-30T16:19:58-0400 rhel9-ctslab-3 pacemakerd[54211]:  error: pacemaker-controld[54218] terminated with signal 6 (Aborted)

We believe this is happening because somehow we're assigning a new value to cib_retry_timer before we run the sleep_timer callback for the first one. So, for example:
1. do_pe_invoke_callback() creates cib_retry_timer. Call it timer-1.
2. do_pe_invoke_callback() creates cib_retry_timer. Call it timer-2. Now cib_retry_timer no longer points to timer-1.
3. sleep_timer gets called for timer-1 . It calls mainloop_timer_del(cib_retry_timer). This destroys timer-2.
4. sleep_timer gets called for timer-2. It calls mainloop_timer_del(cib_retry_timer). This tries to destroy timer-2 again, which fails.

Commit 676b547 removed a blocking wait, so there's probably a way for us to re-enter do_pe_invoke_callback() before the first wait expires.

So I think we should be NULL-ing cib_retry_timer after we delete it, and also making sure it's currently NULL before we assign to it in do_pe_invoke_callback(). We can do this by returning early from do_pe_invoke(). That way we don't lose the reference to our existing timer.

I hope the controller doesn't end up in a busy-loop of just trying to invoke the scheduler over and over until the cib_retry_timer expires. If so, then we'd need to modify whatever code is setting A_PE_INVOKE, or something like that, to try to get the controller to do other useful work.

Even if we're incorrect about the cause of the crashes, this commit seems like a good practice.

Closes T990

This PR renames the app to `VectorTouch` across the project, following the recent repository rename.

The rename is intended to establish a distinct identity for an Android-first experience and avoid confusion with the Android version of GodSVG.

The app has already diverged significantly from the GodSVG, with:
- A complete theme overhaul and UI changes.
- Support for sensor-based orientation (adaptive portrait and landscape modes).
- A mobile friendly TabsPanel designed for touch interactions.
- Touch-optimized interaction patterns, such as replacing hover-based actions with touch based alternatives.

More Android-focused enhancements are planned, and this rename lays the groundwork for treating VectorTouch as Android-first SVG editor.

The implementation includes email/password authentication, guest sessions for cart management, social authentication (Google, Apple), and proper session handling. **Key Features Added:** - Email/password sign-up and sign-in with secure password hashing - Guest sessions that allow users to browse and add items to cart without registration - Guest-to-permanent account conversion while preserving cart data - Social authentication support for Google and Apple OAuth - Comprehensive input validation using Zod schemas - Session management with secure cookies - Route protection and authentication state management - Full TypeScript support with proper typing throughout **Architecture Changes:** - Extended Drizzle schema with Better Auth tables (`users`, `sessions`, `accounts`, `verification`, `guestSessions`) - Created server actions in `src/lib/auth/actions.ts` for all authentication logic - Updated UI components to integrate with server actions - Added authentication hooks, providers, and utility functions - Implemented middleware for session handling ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human This is a **high-risk** change involving authentication, database schema modifications, and new third-party integrations. Please thoroughly test the following: - [ ] **Database Setup**: Configure proper `DATABASE_URL` in production environment and run `npm run db:push` to apply schema changes - [ ] **Authentication Flows**: Test email/password sign-up and sign-in end-to-end, including error handling for invalid credentials and duplicate emails - [ ] **Guest Sessions**: Verify guest users can add items to cart, and test conversion to permanent accounts during checkout/registration - [ ] **Social Authentication**: Set up Google and Apple OAuth credentials in environment variables and test social login flows - [ ] **Session Persistence**: Verify users remain logged in across browser refreshes and that logout properly clears sessions - [ ] **Security**: Test with invalid inputs, SQL injection attempts, and ensure passwords are properly hashed **Recommended Test Plan:** 1. Set up development database with proper connection string 2. Test complete user registration → login → logout flow 3. Test guest cart functionality → account conversion 4. Configure at least one social provider and test OAuth flow 5. Test error scenarios (wrong password, duplicate email, network issues) 6. Verify session cookies are set correctly and persist appropriately --- ### Diagram ```mermaid %%{ init : { "theme" : "default" }}%% graph TD A["src/lib/auth/actions.ts

body:
This pr implements the iterator syntax to support the dynamic creation of benchmark cases at runtime. This allows creating benchmarks for example by

* reading the contents of a file at runtime with each line being a single benchmark case (in contrast to the `file` parameter which parses the file at compile time). The creation of the file can now happen for example during the `setup` and deleted in the `teardown`.
* reading the contents of a directory with each filename being the input of the benchmark, ...
* using ranges `0..=10` and everything that implements `IntoIterator` which is more convenient

The iter syntax will be `#[benches::some_id(iter = 0..5)`

Closes #326
Related #210

body:
This pull request introduces a comprehensive configuration system for the `logfmt` tool, enabling users to customize behavior through a `.logfmt.yaml` file and environment variables. It also adds new commands for configuration management, integrates configuration into existing features, and removes an unused command-line argument. Below are the key changes grouped by theme:

### Configuration System Enhancements:
* Added support for a `.logfmt.yaml` configuration file, allowing customization of output, log processing, fields, worry words, and colors. The configuration file is searched for in the current directory (and upward) or the user's home directory. (`.logfmt.yaml`, `config.go`, [config.goR1-R349](diffhunk://#diff-0e426a43248661127a0c0ee115aef7a1093b635f8993b3f7ebb1dd9f05b8f249R1-R349))
* Introduced a new `--help-config` command to provide detailed help about configuration options. (`cmd.go`, [cmd.goR138-R192](diffhunk://#diff-2d4f0818f10044b5b4b2e35d988be49d71de6e2f9b7b23f996ed3daac8194cb9R138-R192))
* Added `--init-config` and `--init-config-home` commands to create a default configuration file in a specified location or the home directory, respectively. (`cmd.go`, [cmd.goR138-R192](diffhunk://#diff-2d4f0818f10044b5b4b2e35d988be49d71de6e2f9b7b23f996ed3daac8194cb9R138-R192))

### Command-Line Interface Updates:
* Integrated configuration defaults into existing command-line flags, with values loaded from `.logfmt.yaml` or environment variables. (`cmd.go`, [cmd.goR33-R87](diffhunk://#diff-2d4f0818f10044b5b4b2e35d988be49d71de6e2f9b7b23f996ed3daac8194cb9R33-R87))
* Removed the unused `--message-format/-m` argument. (`Changes.md`, [Changes.mdR1-R12](diffhunk://#diff-46efb9fafbbb11cf26bd8ac10f0bc5df02ac0e42f593b87cce382e712b8cf950R1-R12))

### Color and Worry Word Customization:
* Added support for customizable color palettes and worry words through the configuration file. (`config.go`, `.logfmt.yaml`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0e426a43248661127a0c0ee115aef7a1093b635f8993b3f7ebb1dd9f05b8f249R1-R349) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-178a0dcb28d74a4ba54b025b4d8aaa2d78c1556784cf41cb17415f09c41e6f0fR1-R74)
* Updated the `setupColorizer` function to use custom colors if specified in the configuration. (`cmd.go`, [cmd.goR138-R192](diffhunk://#diff-2d4f0818f10044b5b4b2e35d988be49d71de6e2f9b7b23f996ed3daac8194cb9R138-R192))

### Dependency Updates:
* Added dependencies for configuration management, including `viper` and `yaml.v3`. (`go.mod`, [go.modR14-R28](diffhunk://#diff-33ef32bf6c23acb95f5902d7097b7a1d5128ca061167ec0716715b0b9eeaa5f6R14-R28))

### Minor Fixes:
* Corrected a typo in the `IstioDefaultLogLineMatch` regex pattern (`bytesRecieved` → `bytesReceived`). (`parse.go`, [parse.goL84-R84](diffhunk://#diff-1596bd8ceb74246828aacab827b39a33075c86baa627fbbeb7491bd31eef1169L84-R84))

author: sklesse
body:
Hi Andy,

I have added a check whether the rwi dataset has been detrended using difference=T, thus having a grand mean of 0. If so, it needs to be transposed by an arbitrary positive number, otherwise normalize1() messes up the dataset and can divide a series by a slightly negative value, returning false rbar and eps values.

Right now, if people don't pay attention their stats are f***ed up. In 99% of the cases I'd say the normalize1() is not needed, but the easy workaround is to transpose the data if needed. Would be nice if this was an automatic check and operation in the function and dplR library. :-) 

Thx for updating in the next round!
Cheers,
Stefan

body: Updated the memory validation logic in check_for_mem to allow application creation when the available memory size is equal to the required size. Earlier, the validation passed only if available memory was greater than the required size. This caused memory_tests to fail even when exactly 0x2000 bytes were allocated, as defined in the YAML. Changed the condition from greater than to greater than or equal to, so that exact matches are also accepted.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The project was failing to compile with error CS0103: "The name 'DebuggerBrowsableState' does not exist in the current context" in multiple files when Unity is available and all source files are included in the build.

## Root Cause

Four files were using the `DebuggerBrowsable` attribute with `DebuggerBrowsableState` enum values but were missing the required `using System.Diagnostics;` directive:

- `Editor/_b1/_bd8.cs` (line 3383)
- `Editor/_b1/_bh2.cs` (line 676)  
- `Editor/_b1/_bm2.cs` (line 3060)
- `Editor/_b1/_be3.cs` (line 1193)

## Solution

Added the missing `using System.Diagnostics;` directive to each affected file. This is a minimal fix that adds exactly one line per file to resolve the compilation errors.

```csharp
// Before (causing CS0103 error)
[DebuggerBrowsable(DebuggerBrowsableState.Never)]

// After (compiles successfully)
using System.Diagnostics;
// ...
[DebuggerBrowsable(DebuggerBrowsableState.Never)]
```

## Testing

- ✅ Verified all `DebuggerBrowsableState` compilation errors are resolved
- ✅ Confirmed no regressions in existing build configurations
- ✅ Build succeeds both with and without Unity dependencies

This fix ensures the code compiles correctly when Unity is available and all source files are included in the build process.

author: nikilok
body:
when selecting by a specific column and a tie exists, we currently pick by a higher medal and pick the rank.
For example: if your ranking by Bronze, and a tie was discovered we  sort the tied countries by gold, and the higher golds come out on top, but what if their exists a tie in golds ? This PR solves that problem, by recursively going down the other medals like silver and if a tie was found their it goes down to bronze. This way the original order stays unsorted only if a tie breaker wasn't resolved down the medal chain.

author: andybutland
body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I have added steps to test this contribution in the description below

See also: https://github.com/umbraco/Umbraco-CMS/pull/19844

### Description

This extends https://github.com/umbraco/Umbraco-CMS/pull/19657 to add the user start node restrictions (and override via the provided `dataTypeId` parameter for the new "siblings" endpoints).

It follows the patterns established for the "root" and "children" endpoints that already had this functionality in place.

Couple of side-notes:

1. In testing I found an issue with using data types configured to ignore start nodes, and to fix removed this early return from `DateTypeServiceExtensions.IsDataTypeIgnoringUserStartNodes`:

```
  if (DataTypeExtensions.IsBuildInDataType(key))
  {
      return false; // built in ones can never be ignoring start nodes
  }
```

This doesn't seem correct.  Although built-in data types aren't installed with the option to ignore start nodes enabled, there's nothing to stop someone changing this in the data type configuration.

2. I've not concerned myself with breaking changes in this update, as the sibling functionality was created for 16.2, so as long as this is merged in also for 16.2, we don't need to worry about it.

### Testing

Verify that the user start nodes restrictions correctly filter out siblings from the responses, using the integration tests for inspiration on test cases.  Note that the `before` and `after` filters should still be maximally fulfilled if they can be (e.g. given, A, B, C, if requesting C with one before, but B is restricted, A and C should be returned).

Verify that providing the key of a data type configured with ignore user start nodes (e.g. a content picker) means the user start node restrictions aren't applied.

body:
# 🚀 Pull Request – HydrAIDE style

Thanks for contributing to HydrAIDE!
Please fill in the details below so we can review and merge your PR efficiently.

---

## 📋 What does this PR do?

This PR implements a series of CI/CD and contribution experience improvements:

* ✅ Fixes [[#68](https://github.com/hydraide/hydraide/issues/68)](https://github.com/hydraide/hydraide/issues/68): Enables automated Docker image publishing via GitHub Actions on tag push
* ✅ Introduces `pre-commit.ci` as the default pre-commit hook runner for the repo
* ✅ Removes redundant local GitHub Actions CI job for pre-commit checks
* ✅ Restructures the GitHub PR template into `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`
* ✅ Adds `.gitmessage` file with HydrAIDE-specific commit structure guidance
* ✅ Updates `CONTRIBUTING.md` to reflect new workflows and developer practices

With this setup:

* Docker images are automatically built and pushed to GHCR on each `server/v*` tag push
* PR formatting issues are auto-fixed by `pre-commit.ci`
* Contributor onboarding is clearer and streamlined

---

## 🔗 Related Issue(s)

Closes #68

---

## ✅ Checklist

* [x] My code builds and runs locally
* [x] I’ve added tests (if applicable)
* [x] I’ve updated documentation (if needed)
* [x] I’ve reviewed my changes and kept them clean
* [x] This PR is ready for review 🔍

---

## 💬 Additional Notes

* This PR also ensures the Dockerfile no longer relies on secrets if the project is public
* `.env` handling was clarified — it's not needed inside the container; all runtime config is via environment variables
* All changes were validated locally and integrated with the new tag-based release workflow

Thank you for reviewing!

body:
resolves #4704 

Changes in `def identity(...)` in script `preprocessing_functions.py`:
- Metadata fields with types `int`, `float`, or `boolean` are not affected. For example, if `input_datum = " 3"` and the field is expected to be an `int`, the function converts it with `output_datum = int(input_datum)`, resulting in `input_datum = 3`. In this case, stripping whitespace is unnecessary.
- Metadata fields that are `strings` are now cleaned using `.strip() `to remove leading/trailing spaces and newlines.

Changes in `def check_regex(...)` in script `preprocessing_functions.py`:
- The `regex_field` is handled separately in this function (discovered during testing). To avoid mismatches due to whitespace, `regex_field = regex_field.strip()` has been added.

> **⚠️ Note:** Consider adding more fields to testing, to revise all possible options. Currently added `authors` and `regex_field` in Case `strip_spaces_in_metadata`
